## Dieses Dokument

- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.125
- Datum: 8.5.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Wyndham Hotel
42 West 58th street
Newyork, May 8th, 41

Dear Hanna & Manfred,
We have received your letter of April 25th and I am more
than glad that you feel now reassured about Eva. I went to see
her on Sunday and found her well and happy there, and almost
envied her for being there. The house is beautifully situated on
a hill, overlooking other hills and the Hudson river, has large,
if still somewhat neglected, grounds - we realise what it means to
bring even a limited garden back into shape after years of undoubted
neglect. We were all outside in the garden after singing folksongs
at the piano - Eva and Mr. Schaeffer included - and I confirmed
my impression that there are very nice children, especially the boys
and the girl near Eva's age and Mrs. Sch's 3 year old little boy
which is petted and spoiled by all. There is no need for you to
worry about the summer. First of all we have decided not to
go back to Brazil at the present moment but to postpone all
such decision until America's position which seems to get nearer
the war every day, is quite decided. We have vague plans at the
moment to go north to Maine for the summer months, but that
would not worry you as it is not far, according to USA standards,
we would remain in close contact with Eva and might even
have her with us for a while - for I am sure she would not
like to miss the holiday life at Amity Hall to which they
are all looking forward already. The bigger children are all
remaining there for the holidays and others may come, and
they are making all sorts of plans. There seems to be, however
a little misunderstanding between you and Mrs. Sch. I spoke to
her about Eva's learning latin and she said she never wrote
that to you. She or her husband could easily teach Eva but
as she is going to have latin next year anyway if she remains
in USA (and unfortunately, it looks like a long way at present)
she does not think it a very good idea as it would only bore
her once they begin it at school. As regards French, she is ex-
pecting a girl of about 20 or 22 shortly, who has been brought
up in France and will speak French with the children. And as
Eva's friend Marion and her brother speak perfect French too, I
think the prospects for Eva's learning are very good. - Eva had
a very good report for Easter which I am sure she copied for
you. We were happy to learn from your cable that the photos
had safely arrived and that you liked them.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Hotelpapier. Sehr gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
2)
I was terribly sorry to learn that you, Hanna, had trouble
with your teeth and that you have to undergo such a long and
disagreeable treatment. I hope that you are already finished
with it when you get this letter and that you had a well-
deserved rest in Bath in Manfred's company. By the way, how
does your heart stand all this terrible strain. You never men-
tioned it with a single word and I am anxious to learn about
your health more anxious than you need feel about mine.
For I have all the best medical attention and can have all
the rest and quiet and treatments how and when and where I
need it. And over there, rest and quiet in any case cannot always
be easy to find. - We are impatiently looking forward to the day
when Manfred will have finished his exam and come out to
Bath for good or at least find a hospital job in the country.
I have read that the 40 year old have to register for military
service now, but we do not know how soon they are actually
called up and whether physicians will have to do anything out-
side their medical profession. At any rate Manfred ought to take
a good long rest at Bath with you, if possible. You know we
like the idea of knowing you there although it is always with
regret that we cannot be there with you.
Now, Manfred, I think it's just about time to
congratulate you to your birthday and from all my heart
I wish you many happy returns, to be celebrated not only
in Hanna's but also in Eva's and our company. Eva made
me a lovely present, flowers cut out in coloured paper and
glued on cardboard and I am proud how nicely it is done
and how pretty it looks. It is a shame we cannot send
you a present from here, but maybe you see something
which we might have liked to give you and get it in our name.
We are looking forward to Mr. Voge's arrival who, I hope, will
see us immediately and tell us a lot about you.
Kindest regards and best love
Lotte.
Two days ago we sent you the power of attorney
by registered air-mail. Please confirm receipt.
By the way, we have not yet received the
birth and marriage certificates which we may require
for one visa or the other. Did you send them already
or was it not yet possible. Don't take any special trouble,
just let us know about it.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, Fortsetzung auf Seite 2 (hier als Seite 3 im Scan-Set). Sehr gut lesbar.
